new_entities.name: Cognitive behavioral therapy for panic disorder
new_entities.description: Structured CBT using psychoeducation, cognitive restructuring, and exposure-based techniques for panic disorder.

new_entities.name: Panic attack frequency
new_entities.description: How often panic attacks occur over time in people with panic disorder.

edges.effect_quant: A modern network meta-analysis found face-to-face individual CBT superior to treatment as usual for panic disorder efficacy (SMD -0.43, 95% CI -0.70 to -0.15), and an older randomized trial found 85% of treated patients panic-free after group CBT versus 30% of delayed-treatment controls.
edges.population: adolescents and adults with panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia, in randomized CBT trials
edges.mechanism: CBT for panic disorder works by changing catastrophic interpretations of bodily sensations and pairing that cognitive work with interoceptive and situational exposure. As fear of bodily cues drops, panic attacks tend to occur less often and become less disabling.
edges.summary: This is a strong edge. Across older and newer trials, CBT consistently lowers panic symptoms and often meaningfully reduces the recurrence of panic attacks.
edges.caveats: Not every CBT format performs equally well, and some blended or low-adherence formats show weaker results. Comparators also matter: superiority is clearest against treatment as usual, waiting lists, or non-specific control conditions.

evidence.notes: CBT treatment delivery formats for panic disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

effect_quant.comparator: face-to-face individual CBT versus treatment as usual for panic disorder efficacy
